newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to use line-item veto at noon EDT.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to use line-item veto at noon EDT.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will exercise his line-item veto power at noon EDT (1600 GMT) on Monday, the White House said.
Spokesman Mike McCurry would not say which items from recently passed budget legislation would be struck by Clinton, but there were strong indications it would be at least two items.
"He will use the authority. He will use it on both the tax and the spending measures," McCurry told reporters.

Prime candidates were reportedly a change in the Medicaid programme that the Clinton administration considered flawed policy, as well as a provision worth an estimated $84 million over five years that would allow the deferral of taxes for the sale of a food-processing plant to farmers' cooperatives.
The line-item veto allows a president to block parts of spending bills or strike down narrowly targeted tax breaks without vetoing entire bills.

Congress has often tacked special provisions onto otherwise unrelated bills, leaving the president little choice. Any veto Clinton makes will likely face a court challenge over the constitutionality of the line-item veto.
